# Season 2 day-152 planning check-in (~Jun 1, 10 trips booked so far, rank 4/34 at 0.6281)

## CRITICAL budget correction — the old "save for fall day_1_5" plan is DEAD
I've spent $1500 of $2000 on ten $150 three_quarter probes (d099-150), only **$500 left**, 10/10 PTO
still banked. **DAY_1_5 costs $550 — I literally cannot afford even one anymore unless I stop ALL
other spending right now.** Overnight ($400) is affordable exactly once if nothing else is bought.
Forget the Season-1-derived plan of banking budget for an Oct/Nov day_1_5 blitz — it's not
realistic from here. **Three_quarter ($150) is now the only class I can responsibly run more than
once or twice more, and it stays the core weapon through November, not just April-June.**

## ONI still recovering, roughly on schedule
Season 2 ONI: d9=-1.57, d40=-1.48, d71=-1.29, d99=-1.06, **d130=-0.85**. Steady ~+0.2/30days
improvement, unchanged pace since day91 check-in. Extrapolating: ~-0.6 by Aug, ~-0.3 to -0.15 by
Oct, maybe touching neutral around Nov. Still not clearly "recovered" but the trend is intact —
keep logging each new monthly ONI print and compare against realized 3Q rates below.

## Season-2 3Q rate IS recovering, San Diego confirmed the boat to ride
Rough month-bucket check (bucket = (doy-1)//30.5, so bucket3≈May, bucket4≈June(doy124-154)):
season-2 3Q rate bucket3(May)=0.069(n=71 boat-trips) → bucket4(Jun-to-date)=**0.153(n=71)** — real
improvement, consistent with San Diego's trailing rate. Same recovery pattern shows for
overnight (bucket3=0.011→bucket4=0.161) but day_1_5 stayed flat/tiny (bucket4=0.024, n=11, too
thin to read). **Caveat: my bucket math is a rough (doy-1)//30.5 approximation and does NOT
cleanly match my old Season-1 calendar-month table (Apr/May/Jun/Jul numbers came out different
here) — treat this bucket analysis as a same-season trend check only, don't reconcile it against
the old Season-1-by-name-month numbers, they're not computed the same way.**
- **Boat ranking, trailing 14 days (doy138-152), three_quarter:** San Diego 0.396 (n=10 boat-trips,
  346 anglers) clearly best and well-sampled. Mission Belle 0.221 (n=7) second. Malihini has
  cooled to 0.145 (n=11). Everything else near/at zero or n≤2 (noise). **San Diego stays the
  default probe target; recheck Mission Belle if San Diego ever cools for 3+ trips.**
- fishdope: migrated=True every recent day, yt_all trending up (3→...→11 by d152), yt_local still
  modest (0-2/day) — a real but modest ongoing signal, matches the boat-level recovery.

## New finding: overnight/day_1_5 look MORE La-Niña-suppressed than 3Q this season, not less
Season-2-to-date totals vs Season-1-to-date-same-window: 3Q ~2.5x suppressed recently (0.153 vs
0.379 Season-1 same bucket), but **overnight is ~10x suppressed overall (0.042 vs 0.419 season
totals) and day_1_5 ~15x (0.030 vs 0.457)** — though both on thin n (93 and 51 boat-trips for the
whole season so far). This is a real caution flag against assuming Season 1's "Oct/Nov day_1_5
blows everything else away" pattern repeats this year. Even if budget allowed it, don't assume
day_1_5/overnight will out-earn 3Q in fall this season — **re-pull this same
Season1-vs-Season2 suppression-ratio comparison once real Sept/Oct data exists before ever sizing
up into a multi-day trip.**

## PTO: stop treating it as scarce — it's the budget that's tight now, not PTO
10/10 PTO still unused because I've only fired on no-PTO-cost weekends/holidays. That was the
right caution when I still hoped to save PTO for a big fall day_1_5. That plan is dead (see
above), so PTO is now nearly free optionality: **allow committing PTO (14 days ahead) for a
WEEKDAY three_quarter trip when the target boat's trailing ~14-day rate is clearly elevated
(≳0.25-0.3, decent n) — don't wait for a weekend just because that's the habit.** Missing a
midweek hot streak because "no PTO committed" is a pure unforced loss now that PTO has no
opportunity cost left to protect.

## Revised plan for the nightly self, rest of season (Jun-Nov)
1. **Keep three_quarter as the only real lever.** Book San Diego (or whichever boat leads the
   trailing ~14-day rate, min n≈5) when that rate is at/above ~0.15-0.2 (roughly the current
   recovering baseline) OR fishdope shows a fresh yt_all/migrated spike. Skip when the leading
   boat's trailing rate has fallen back near/at zero for 3+ trips with no fresh report signal.
2. **Weekday trips are now OK, not just weekend/holiday freebies** — see PTO note above. Still
   prefer weekend/holiday (0 PTO cost) when the signal is only moderate; spend PTO only when the
   signal is genuinely strong.
3. **Budget pacing for the remaining $500:** don't fire every single available weekend through the
   likely-weak Jul-Sep window (Season-1 pattern says Jul-Sep is the weakest stretch; watch if
   Season-2 repeats that once the data posts). Target roughly 1 confirmed-signal probe every 1-2
   weeks through summer (~$150-300 total for Jul-Sep), keeping **at least $200-250 in reserve
   for Oct-Nov**, when 3Q historically firms up again and ONI should be closer to neutral.
   Re-evaluate the exact split once Jul/Aug/Sep Season-2 rates actually post.
4. If, and only if, budget is sitting near/above $400 in Sept/Oct AND a boat/class shows a
   genuinely large recent spike (well above anything seen this season, e.g. San Diego trailing
   >0.4-0.5 over a real sample), a single overnight ($400) could be worth the swing — but this is
   now a rare opportunistic bet, not a planned centerpiece. Do NOT plan around it.
5. HD_AM/HD_PM: still hard-avoid, reconfirm remains ~dead if convenient but no need to keep
   re-querying every night — this has been true all season and structurally (per old Season-1
   review) half-days are ~15-20x worse per dollar than 3Q even in good years.
6. Standing: rank 4/34 at 0.6281 season score, tied with 3 others just below me; leader
   (calendarist) at 0.7045, only ~0.076 ahead — roughly one good 3Q trip's worth of share. Worth
   staying selectively active rather than going fully passive for the rest of the year.
7. strategy.py stays the placeholder (books nothing) — nightly manual judgment has been driving
   every actual booking all season and that's working fine; no need to encode reflexes in code
   given how much this depends on reading the live trailing-rate signal each night.

## Open questions for the next planning turn
- Did Jul-Sep Season-2 3Q/overnight rates crater like Season-1's did, or does the ONI recovery
  keep them elevated relative to Season-1's same window (as bucket4 vs bucket3 already hinted)?
- Did the overnight/day_1_5 suppression ratio (10-15x) narrow once more Sept/Oct data exists, or
  is it a real feature of this La Niña year (multi-day trips need warmer water/more range than
  3Q's inshore grounds)? This determines whether a fall overnight bet is ever worth the $400.
- Recompute real calendar-month rates properly (not my rough doy//30.5 bucketing) if a cleaner
  month field becomes available — the bucket numbers here disagreed with my old Season-1 monthly
  table in a way that suggests boundary smearing, not necessarily a real pattern change.
- Track budget precisely each check-in: at this pace (10 trips/$1500 in ~53 days) I will run out
  well before November if I don't slow down now that the day_1_5 cushion is gone.

# Season 2 day-121 planning check-in (May 1, ~1 month of nightly decisions done)
- **Cold-ONI hypothesis CONFIRMED with real data.** ONI trend: -1.57(d9)→-1.48(d40)→-1.29(d71)→
  -1.06(d99) — recovering but still deep La Niña. Season 2 Apr-Jun three_quarter rate so far =
  0.066 yt/angler (n=77) vs Season 1's Apr-Jun 0.469 (n=312) — ~7x suppression (see day-152 update
  above: suppression has since narrowed to ~2.5x as of June).
- Status at the time: $1200/$2000 spent, 0/10 PTO, season_score 0.6117, rank 2/34.
- San Diego was already the best 3Q boat (0.110/21d) vs Mission Belle (0.092) vs Malihini (0.031);
  still true as of d152 (San Diego 0.396/14d vs Mission Belle 0.221 vs Malihini 0.145).
- HD_AM/HD_PM reconfirmed dead (0.0008/angler over 108 boat-trips) — still true, hard-avoid.
- The plan written here to "protect $800+10 PTO for Oct-Nov day_1_5" is **superseded** by the
  day-152 update above: budget ran down faster than planned (10 probes instead of fewer), and
  day_1_5/overnight are now both unaffordable-or-nearly and looking more La-Niña-suppressed than
  3Q this season anyway.

# Notes after Season 1 review (carried forward reference numbers, treat as an upper-bound prior
# only — Season 2's La Niña has suppressed most classes well below these so far)

## Big finding: half-days are nearly dead for yellowtail (still true, structural)
hd_am: 94% zero trips, 0.013/angler. hd_pm: 93% zero, 0.014/angler. three_quarter: 51% zero,
0.245/angler — ~18x the half-day rate for <2x the price. overnight: 62% zero, 0.356/angler.
day_1_5: 75% zero, 0.477/angler (highest raw rate, priciest). Ranked $/fish: three_quarter >
overnight ≈ day_1_5 >> half-days. **Three_quarter is the cheap-ticket workhorse, half-days are a
trap for this species regardless of price.**

## Season-1 calendar-month reference table (an upper bound this La Niña year, not a baseline)
Apr: 3Q 0.56, overnight 1.27, day_1_5 1.93 (best month). May: 3Q 0.54, overnight 0.40, day_1_5
0.44. Jun: 3Q 0.46, overnight 0.60, day_1_5 0.18. Jul-Sep: craters across the board (3Q 0.04-0.06,
overnight 0.02-0.24). Oct: BIG rebound, day_1_5 2.35, 3Q 0.31, overnight 0.69. Nov: day_1_5 1.86
still strong, 3Q/overnight fade to 0.06-0.13.

## Boats (three_quarter, Season-1 Apr-Jun, n≥5, for reference)
San Diego (n=81, rate 0.61), Mission Belle (n=61, rate 0.55), Malihini (n=73, rate 0.44). Pacific
Voyager/Voyager had high rates but tiny n (7-8) — never repeated in Season 2, treat as noise.

## To check every nightly briefing (Apr-Nov) — unchanged
1. fishdope yt_local/yt_all/migrated/stamp_kind — fresh local push overrides seasonal averages.
2. Trailing ~14-day rate for the SPECIFIC boat being considered (min n≈5-10), not just class avg.
3. Water temp (pier wtmp_c) trend as a leading signal.
4. ONI — log every new monthly print, compare against realized 3Q/overnight/day_1_5 rates.
5. PTO 14-day lock-in — now OK to spend on a confirmed weekday hot streak (see day-152 update),
   not just reserved for a fall day_1_5 that's no longer affordable.
